textContent.text: Zane glanced at his watch and gasped. "I'm late!" he blurted, running toward the park gate. His backpack bounced wildly as he raced past the swings and onto the sidewalk. He ran as fast as he could, nearly knocking over his principal, Mrs. Hendry.
"Sorry, Mrs. Hendry," Zane called over his shoulder as he dashed past.
"Woah!" said Mrs. Hendry, watching him disappear around a corner.
At home, Zane skidded through the front door just as Mom set dinner on the table. "Made it!" he said.
"Barely," Mom teased.
The next morning, Mrs. Hendry was waiting for Zane at school.
"I'm sorry I ran into you," Zane said.
"Never mind that," Mrs. Hendry said. "After yesterday, I want you to sign up for the track team!"

content.text: What is most likely true about Mrs. Hendry?

choices.text: She's impressed by how fast Zane can run.
She's worried Zane might trip and hurt himself.
She's annoyed that Zane nearly knocked her over.

textContent.text: A low hum filled the room as red warning lights blinked on Father's computer screen. He leaned back, squinting at the screen. "A meteor shower is coming," he said. "Should be here in twenty minutes."
Alan's eyes widened. "What do we do?"
Father smiled. "We've got plenty of time," he said, handing Alan a key. "Now, get the rover and park it in the cave so it won't get dented by space rocks."
Next, Father turned to Geoff. "As for you, go round up the astro cows and put them in the barn. Let's meet back here in ten."
The boys looked up. "Shouldn't we take cover?" Alan asked.
Father gave a quick grin. "No, we've got plenty of time. Let's play one round of digital cards before the storm hits!"

textContent.text: Deidre carefully stacked the cans, one on top of the other. It was her first day working at the grocery store, and she wanted to impress her manager, Mrs. Benson. Deidre had just placed the final can on the top of the display when a voice called out.
"Hey, Deidre!"

Startled, Deidre whipped around. As she turned, her hip knocked into the perfect pyramid of cans. CRASH! The pyramid fell and cans rolled everywhere. Horrified, Deidre looked up to see Mrs. Benson coming toward her.
"Mrs. Benson, I am so sorry," Deidre began. But she hesitated when she saw that Mrs. Benson was laughing.
"Well done!" Mrs. Benson said. "We need to see exactly how many cans you knocked over. You may have broken my own record!"
